target.name: the bossman
target.detail: watching the football, not the door

setup: Corner shop, one bored bossman with the football on the little telly behind the counter, blind spot by the fridges.
on_success: Half-time whistle, you're out the door. He never looks up from the replay.
on_fail: Turns out he watches the mirror during the ads. 'Oi — pockets.' Bag search energy. You bounce.
on_crit: You clear the top shelf by the fridges. Whole armful. He'd have caught it if City weren't two-nil down.

setup: Big supermarket, self-checkout, one tired member of staff covering eight machines and a queue of beeping.
on_success: Half of it scanned, half of it not. The machine trusts you. That's its whole problem.
on_fail: 'Unexpected item in the bagging area' — and this time she comes over, and this time she checks.
on_crit: You weigh a bag of loose sweets as onions and the machine agrees enthusiastically. Trolley's worth, paid for pennies.

setup: Chemist, half the good stuff behind those magnetic tags, one security guard on his phone by the exit.
on_success: Tags off in the aisle, product in the coat, out past the guard as he laughs at something on his screen.
on_fail: You miss a tag. The gate screams. The guard finally has a reason to exist and he's thrilled about it.
on_crit: Whole basket of the pricey stuff. Perfume, razors, the lot. The tag machine was in the same unlocked drawer as the tags.

target.detail: changing room, four items in, two out

setup: High street clothes shop, changing rooms with a bored attendant counting hangers, not counting closely.
on_success: Four in, two out, two on under your own coat. The maths only works if someone's checking. Nobody's checking.
on_fail: The attendant counts hangers for a living and today she's decided to be good at it. 'That's four you took in.'
on_crit: You layer up in the cubicle like it's winter. Walk out padded, walk home rich, peel it all off at the fence.

setup: Market stall, phones and chargers and knock-off everything, one man serving three customers and losing.
on_success: In the chaos of change and 'have you got it in black,' a handful walks. He's still counting coins wrong.
on_fail: The man beside him — the one you didn't clock — is the one who actually watches the goods. And he's watching you.
on_crit: You lift a boxed set while he argues a refund. Sealed, sellable, straight to Keisha. Beautiful timing.

target.detail: buzzer on the door, camera that maybe works

setup: Off-licence, late, buzzer door, one camera in the corner that may or may not be plugged into anything.
on_success: You test the camera theory. The camera theory holds. Out the buzzer door with a full coat.
on_fail: The camera was real and so was the panic button. Shutters start coming down. You just make the gap.
on_crit: Whole shelf of the good spirits. The camera was a dummy. You knew it. You could tell. You got lucky, is what.

target.detail: power tools, orange aprons, acres of aisle

setup: Big orange DIY warehouse, power tools worth proper money, staff spread thin across aisles the size of streets.
on_success: Drill in the trolley, drill out to the car park like you own a house. Nobody stops a man who looks busy.
on_fail: The tool aisles are exactly where they put the cameras and the one keen lad on his first week.
on_crit: Two cordless sets and a nail gun. You wheel it out with a receipt for a bag of screws. Confidence is a tool too.

target.name: Sanjay
target.detail: watching pump four, not the aisles

setup: Petrol station shop, one man watching for drive-offs on the forecourt, back turned to the aisles behind him.
on_success: While he's squinting at a car on pump four, the meal deals and the energy drinks migrate into your bag.
on_fail: He's got eyes in the back of his head and a mate on the forecourt. Both of them clock you at once.
on_crit: Forecourt kicks off — someone actually does drive off — and in the chaos you clear a whole shelf. Terrible day for Sanjay.

setup: Quiet bookshop, carpet that eats sound, one member of staff shelving at the far end, lost in the alphabet.
on_success: You browse honestly for ten minutes, then not honestly for ten seconds. Coat's heavier on the way out.
on_fail: The quiet cuts both ways — she hears the tag-strip tear from three aisles over and knows exactly what it means.
on_crit: Nice hardbacks, the collectable kind. Keisha'll know someone. Even the crime does crime in here, apparently.

target.detail: a sale sign and a scrum

setup: Sale on, shop rammed, a scrum round the discount bins, staff drowning, alarms half-ignored from all the false ones.
on_success: You go with the crowd, take with the crowd, leave before the crowd. Nobody remembers one more elbow.
on_fail: A store detective works exactly this kind of chaos, and she's been doing it since before you were born.
on_crit: In the crush you fill a bag they'd normally search, and walk out past a queue too long for anyone to check.
